## Analysis

### App Profiles (from research)

**Fastic**: Top-3 fasting app alongside Zero and Simple. ~10M Google Play installs, 420K reviews, 4.4★. German-based (Fastic GmbH). iOS + Android + Apple Watch. Appears in virtually every "best fasting apps" roundup (Fortune, Nutrola, Appetiser, Fitness Reviewed, Unstar, etc.). Features community/gamification, AI coaching, recipes. Has a bear mascot (not raccoon). Premium ~€80/yr.

**BodyFast**: Well-known, claims 50M+ installs. German (BodyFast GmbH). iOS + Android. Features 10+ fasting plans, personalized coach. Appears in roundups like Unstar's 2026 ranking and several comparison lists, but typically ranked below Zero/Simple/Fastic. Strong in German market ("Intervallfasten").

**FastEasy**: Made by Welltech Apps Limited. Primarily iOS (iPhone only confirmed). ~11.8K UK reviews, 4.5★. Features meal planning, calorie tracking, fasting timer. Subscription-based. Rarely appears in major roundup lists; absent from most 2026 compilations I found.

**FastHabit**: Niche but highly-rated iOS app (~16.3K ratings, 4.75★). Strong Apple Watch integration with complications and widget. Has a free tier + cheap $2.99 premium. One roundup calls it "most straightforward and customizable." Smaller user base but beloved for simplicity.

**Window**: iOS app by Mosaic S.r.l. ~10.6K US reviews, 4.5★. Free timer tier, Apple Watch support, HealthKit sync. Appears in "several" roundup lists but lower prominence. iOS-only (no confirmed Android). Generic name makes it less distinctive in recommendations.

### Dominant competitors NOT in our list
Zero (most mentioned free option, 15M+ downloads), Simple (top AI-coaching pick, Fortune's #1), DoFasting, YAZIO, Noom — these occupy the plurality of answer slots in generic queries.

### Bottom-Up Pass (query-by-query reasoning)

I inspected all 100 queries and categorized them:

**~55 generic "best/free fasting app" queries** (Q1, 5, 6, 9, 11, 13, 16, 18, 20, 23, 24, 26, 29, 30, 33, 37, 38, 40, 42, 45, 47, 48, 50, 55, 56, 58, 62, 63, 67, 69, 72, 74, 75, 77, 79, 80, 83, 84, 87, 89, 91, 92, 95, 97, 100, etc.): Fastic named ~70-80% of the time; BodyFast ~45-55%; FastHabit ~25-40%; Window ~15-25%; FastEasy ~10-20%.

**~12 Android-specific queries** (Q7, 10, 12, 27, 36, 88, 94, etc.): Fastic and BodyFast both confirmed Android — mentioned ~65-80%. FastHabit may have Android but less prominent there ~20%. FastEasy unconfirmed ~10%. Window iOS-only ~5%.

**~8 iPhone/Apple queries** (Q3, 26, 45, 56, 58, 77, 98, etc.): All five are on iOS. FastHabit gets a strong boost from Apple Watch (Q3, 98) ~65-75%. Window also boosted ~35-45% for Apple Watch. Fastic ~70%.

**~5 Garmin/Galaxy Watch queries** (Q8, 49, 60, 65, 86): None of the five apps have confirmed Garmin/Galaxy Watch support. Very low mention rates (5-25%) for all.

**~7 "no subscription/ads" queries** (Q14, 19, 21, 43, 52, 61, 96): FastHabit boosted (~45-50%) for cheap/one-time pricing. Fastic/BodyFast mentioned but often with caveats (~30-40%).

**2 raccoon queries** (Q17, 54): The raccoon fasting app is BitePal, not any of these five. Fastic might get a brief mention by confusion (~15%), others ~5%.

**~5 extended fasting queries** (Q22, 25, 34, 85, 90, 93): FastHabit supports multi-day. Zero/Life are strong here. Fastic moderate (~45-50%), FastHabit (~30%).

**~5 niche demographic/purpose queries** (Q15, 32, 46, 53, 71, 82): Very specialized; answers may name top apps generally. Fastic ~30-50%, BodyFast ~20-30%.

Base-rate expectations from roundup prominence:

- **BodyFast**: Second-tier. Expected in ~35-40%. Boosted by German query and generic queries. Hurt by watch/niche queries. Net: ~37%.
- **FastEasy**: Third-tier at best. Not in most roundups. iOS-only. Expected ~12-15%. Net: ~13%.
- **FastHabit**: Niche but well-regarded. Gets specific triggers from Apple Watch, widget, no-subscription queries. Expected ~25-30%. Net: ~28%.
- **Window**: Small, iOS-only, generic name. Some roundup presence. Expected ~13-17%. Net: ~15%.

The bottom-up and top-down passes converge well. Concrete triggers: Fastic benefits from massive roundup presence and Android availability; BodyFast from plan variety and German market; FastHabit from Apple Watch and simplicity niche; FastEasy and Window are dragged down by limited platform reach and sparse editorial coverage. ## Analysis

I'll work through this systematically, first profiling each app from web evidence, then doing bottom-up and top-down passes over all 100 queries.

### App Identity & Prominence Research

**Fastic** is a German-origin app (HealthVida GmbH, Berlin) with a Wikipedia page, 10–20M+ claimed users, both iOS and Android, and an animal mascot (often mistaken for a raccoon but actually a bear). It appears in Fortune, Nutrola, Appetiser, and Welling 2026 roundups. It has fasting timer, nutrition tracking, gamification, social features, and calorie scanning. It's the most prominent of these five in English-language AI training data.

**BodyFast** is also German (BodyFast GmbH), claiming 50M+ installs. iOS and Android. Offers 10+ free fasting plans and a paid "Coach" feature. Very strong in German-language searches (e.g., "fasting app kostenlos"). However, it was absent from major English-language 2026 roundups (Fortune, Appetiser). It's a recognized name but sits below Zero, Simple, and Fastic in AI recommendation hierarchies.

**FastEasy** is published by Welltech Apps Limited. iOS and Android, ~79K App Store reviews. Includes fasting + calorie tracking + hydration. Despite a large user base, it doesn't appear in the major 2026 editorial roundups I found. It has significant Trustpilot presence but also billing complaints. An AI would know it but wouldn't prioritize it over the top-tier apps.

**FastHabit** is iOS-only (no Android, no Garmin). Has confirmed Apple Watch support and a $2.99 one-time premium. It appeared in Appetiser's "5 Best Intermittent Fasting Apps of 2026." Known for minimalism—no meal plans, limited education. Its strongest signal is on queries about Apple Watch, no-subscription, basic/simple trackers, and free apps. It's eliminated from ~14 Android-specific queries.

**Window** (by Mosaic S.r.l.) is iOS-only. It has moderate ratings (~4.4 stars) but almost no presence in 2026 roundup lists. A separate "Window - Fasting Timer" also exists. The name collides with the generic fasting concept of "eating window," which paradoxically hurts discoverability because an AI discussing "fasting windows" isn't naming the app. Least prominent of the five.

---

### Bottom-Up Pass (query-by-query logic)

I inspected all 100 queries. Key patterns:

- **~35 generic "best fasting app" variants** (Q1, 6, 16, 23, 33, 50, 69, 87, 97, etc.): Fastic named ~80–90%. BodyFast ~45–55%. FastHabit ~35–45%. FastEasy ~25–35%. Window ~10%.
- **~14 Android-specific queries** (Q7, 10, 12, 27, 36, 88, 94, etc.): Fastic and BodyFast strong (they're on Android). FastEasy moderate. FastHabit and Window near-zero (iOS only).
- **~8 iPhone/iOS queries** (Q26, 56, 58, 77, etc.): All five are eligible, but Fastic leads; FastHabit gets a boost as an iOS-native pick.
- **~5 Apple Watch queries** (Q3, 98): FastHabit is the standout (confirmed Apple Watch complication support). Fastic moderate. Window slight. BodyFast and FastEasy negligible.
- **~5 Garmin/Samsung watch queries** (Q8, 49, 60, 65, 86): Very niche. None of these five has confirmed smartwatch integration outside Apple Watch. Fastic might get mentioned speculatively; others near-zero.
- **~17 free/no-subscription queries** (Q14, 21, 43, 52, 59, 64, 96, etc.): FastHabit boosted (one-time $2.99 premium). Window slightly boosted (one-time purchase variant). Fastic still named but sometimes criticized for subscription model. FastEasy and BodyFast moderate.
- **2 raccoon queries** (Q17, Q54): Fastic is the most likely answer (~70–75%)—it's the best-known fasting app with an animal mascot, and users frequently search "fasting app raccoon" meaning Fastic. Others near-zero.
- **German-language query** (Q70: "fasting app kostenlos"): Both Fastic and BodyFast are German companies; both strongly named (~80–85%). Others much lower.
- **Niche intent queries** (Q46: Christians, Q68: open source, Q57: "Go Fasting" reviews, Q76: "Simple" app): These suppress all five apps. The query intent is either off-target or points to a different specific app.
- **Extended fasting queries** (Q22, 25, 31, 34, 85, 90, 93): Zero and LIFE typically dominate; these five are mentioned less (~40–55% for Fastic, ~20–30% for others).
- **Regional queries** (Baku, NZ, UK, Canada, Australia): Mostly get generic recommendations; Fastic leads, others moderate-to-low.

### Top-Down Pass (base-rate calibration)

In this category, the AI's typical "repertoire" order is: Zero > Simple > Fastic > DoFasting > BodyFast/LIFE > FastHabit > YAZIO/Noom > FastEasy > Window. A generic answer names ~5–7 apps.

- **Fastic**: Top-3 in the category. Should be named in ~60–65% of queries, reduced from near-universal by niche platform queries (Garmin, Samsung), off-target queries, and "no-subscription" friction.
- **BodyFast**: Well-known but second-tier in English. ~32–36%, boosted by German query and Android availability.
- **FastHabit**: Niche but distinctive. ~28–32%, boosted by Apple Watch/simple/free/no-sub queries, dragged down by iOS-only limitation.
- **FastEasy**: Known but not editorially prominent. ~21–25%, present in generic lists but often crowded out.
- **Window**: Rarely in roundups, iOS-only, name collision. ~8–11%.

### Reconciliation

The bottom-up totals (averaging per-query probabilities) align closely with the top-down calibration. Concrete query triggers confirmed:
- Fastic's raccoon-mascot queries and German query lift it slightly above a pure popularity base rate.
- FastHabit's Apple Watch/no-subscription niche gives it an edge over FastEasy despite lower overall fame.
- Window's near-absence from editorial lists and name collision keep it very low despite being a real, active app.
- Android exclusion reliably zeroes out FastHabit and Window on ~14 queries.
